root_cause.text: When ctnetlink creates an expectation via netlink without the CTA_EXPECT_NAT attribute, the NAT-related fields (saved_addr, saved_proto, dir) are left uninitialized because they are allocated from a non-zeroing slab cache, allowing stale data from a prior slab occupant to be leaked to userspace during a subsequent dump.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "ctnetlink_alloc_expect() allocates expectations from a non-zeroing slab cache via nf_ct_expect_alloc(). When CTA_EXPECT_NAT is not present in the netlink message, saved_addr and saved_proto are never initialized. Stale data from a previous slab occupant can then be dumped to userspace by ctnetlink_exp_dump_expect()". The patch adds explicit zeroing of these fields in the else branch under `#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_NF_NAT)`.

bic_trace_step.reason: In ctnetlink_create_expect (lines ~1480-1520), after allocating the expectation with nf_conntrack_expect_alloc, the code sets exp->expectfn, exp->flags, and exp->master, and copies the tuple and mask, but does not initialize any NAT-related fields (saved_addr, saved_proto, dir). Since the expectation is allocated from a non-zeroing slab cache, these fields contain stale data from prior use. No CTA_EXPECT_NAT attribute exists in this commit, so all expectations are created without NAT initialization. This constitutes the vulnerable construct described. The dump function (ctnetlink_exp_dump_expect) does not include these NAT fields, so a leak is not yet possible, but the uninitialized data remains a bug.
